notes: Decompiled Minecraft sources: .abacusai/temp/mcsrc (105 files) + the NeoForm sources jar in the gradle cache
Verified: RenderTarget.bindWrite() does NOT clear; TextureTarget defaults to a WHITE clear colour
Verified: SingleQuadParticle.render() is overridable -> a flat XZ quad is possible for the ripple rings
Verified: NeoForge 1.21.1 has NO entity-entered-fluid event -> the impact detector is client-side
Verified: the vanilla sun is a 60x60 quad at distance 100 with a 14px white square in a 32px texture (~15 deg across)
Verified: ParticleRenderType.PARTICLE_SHEET_TRANSLUCENT draws AFTER the translucent chunk layer, so ripples land on top of the water
Tuning knobs: SunRenderer.DISC_ANGLE / CORONA_ANGLE (sun size), GodRayRenderer BASE_INTENSITY and the two exposures (shaft strength)
Open: the sun's disc radius is seeded at 1.5x the drawn disc so a canopy's gaps can seed the shafts
The shadow pass is the expensive part: 2 extra chunk layers over the near sections, every other frame
MC view bobbing is applied to the projection matrix in GameRenderer.renderLevel - anything computed from it rocks with the walk cycle
The shadow map is now 224 blocks across (112 either side) so it reaches the cloud layer
Minecraft.isPaused() is only true for a singleplayer pause screen - in multiplayer the world keeps running, which is correct
CelestialLight.NIGHT_DARKEN = 0.42 and MOON_STRENGTH = 0.20 are the two numbers to tune
The SSR pass is half resolution - full resolution would sharpen the player reflection but costs 4x
